# Parent-drift breadcrumb comment (echo-safe, nearest-represented-ancestor)

## Context / Problem

When a local parent relationship cannot be represented in Jira — the parent is a
non-epic and this next-gen project permits only Epic parents — the outbound differ
already **suppresses the parent field** before it is ever sent
(`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:196-215`: `parent_id in local_ticket_types` and
`parent_type != "epic"` ⇒ the parent diff is dropped and reported on the
`dropped_field_sink` / `suppressed_out` channel). The child then lands in Jira as an
under-defined leaf: the Jira user sees no hint that its defining parent context lives
elsewhere. Alt-link self-heal was rejected as echo-unsafe. We need an **echo-safe
breadcrumb comment** that points the Jira user at the nearest ancestor that *is* visible
in Jira, without ever being re-ingested inbound as user content.

## Approach

Emit the breadcrumb from the **outbound comment differ**, where every input the
mechanism needs is already in scope, rather than from the apply-time alert recorder
`pass_io.record_parent_divergence` (which carries only scalar strings — see Scope).
Integrate it into `outbound_comments._diff_comments` (`outbound_comments.py:385`), which
already: (a) resolves the complete Jira comment list for the child (`jira_comments`,
from the snapshot or, when the snapshot lacks the `comment` field, one bounded
`client.get_comments` live fetch — the bug-4292 safety invariant); (b) builds the
marker-stripped normalized body set `jira_bodies` used for dedup; (c) holds the
`binding_store` and the `TicketTransport` `client`. Reusing the already-resolved
`jira_comments` avoids a second fetch (honoring the bounded-call invariant).

On a bound child whose direct parent is type-collapsed (the exact suppression condition
above), walk the ancestor chain upward and name the **nearest ancestor with a bound Jira
key**. Build the body on the existing managed-comment machinery: decorate it with
`RECONCILER_MARKER` via `_decorate_outbound_comment` (`outbound_comments.py:209`) and
return it as an ordinary `{"action": "add", ...}` comment mutation appended to
`_diff_comments`' result, so it is posted through the existing comment enactment path
(`dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_dispatch_comments:347` → `client.add_comment`,
implemented by both the ACLI and Data Center backends — `adapters/jira/backend.py:361`,
`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:558`).

**Echo-safety (corrected).** The breadcrumb is a comment we *do* want mirrored to Jira,
so it must **not** be recognized by `_is_machine_marker_comment`
(`outbound_comments.py:375-382`) — that predicate matches only
`_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` (`'BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:'`, `'Still stale as of'`) and would
*exclude* a comment from being sent outbound, the opposite of what we want; the
breadcrumb body therefore starts with neither prefix. Instead, echo-safety on the
*inbound* side is provided by the `RECONCILER_MARKER` substring check in
`inbound_collection_diffs._diff_comments_inbound` (`inbound_collection_diffs.py:154`:
`if RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text: continue`), which skips any Jira comment carrying the
marker so our own breadcrumb is never pulled back in as a user comment. Note that
`_normalize_comment_body` (`outbound_comments.py:184-206`) **strips** `RECONCILER_MARKER`
before classification/dedup, so the marker itself can never make
`_is_machine_marker_comment` fire and does not participate in the body-equality key — it
serves only the inbound suppression at line 154 and the send-path fit preservation
(`fit_preserving_marker`).

**Append-once / supersede.** Dedup on a **stable breadcrumb identity tag**
(`<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->`, a constant substring), not on the variable ancestor
key: before appending, scan the resolved `jira_comments` (marker-stripped via
`_normalize_comment_body`, which does *not* strip the breadcrumb tag) for that tag; if
any existing comment already carries it, emit nothing. This makes the breadcrumb
append-once **and** robust to the cross-pass staleness concern: if the nearest
represented ancestor later changes, tag-based dedup still sees a breadcrumb present and
appends **no** second, conflicting comment (first-writer-wins). Because the outbound
comment path is **ADD-only** (`_diff_comments` emits only `"add"`; there is no
transport-portable comment edit/delete), the original breadcrumb is intentionally not
rewritten — an accepted limitation stated below. This is a positive fit for the problem:
it reuses the existing, well-tested comment differ and its fetch-safety invariant, adds
no new transport capability, and cannot loop.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py` — add a pure breadcrumb
  builder `_build_parent_breadcrumb(...)` and integrate it into `_diff_comments`
  (`outbound_comments.py:385`): after `jira_bodies` is built, when the drift condition
  holds and no resolved Jira comment carries the `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` tag,
  append one decorated `"add"` mutation. New `_diff_comments` params: `local_parents`
  (`{local_id -> parent_id}`) and `local_ticket_types` (`{local_id -> ticket_type}`),
  both defaulting to `None` (no breadcrumb when absent — preserves every existing
  caller/test). Reuses `RECONCILER_MARKER`, `_decorate_outbound_comment`,
  `_normalize_comment_body`, and the already-resolved `jira_comments`/`jira_bodies`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py` — in
  `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` (`outbound_mutation_builders.py:163`), pass the
  new `local_parents` argument (threaded from the caller) and the already-in-scope
  `local_ticket_types` into the `_diff_comments(...)` call
  (`outbound_mutation_builders.py:277`).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — in
  `compute_outbound_mutations` (`outbound_differ.py:449`), build a `local_parents` map
  `{t["ticket_id"]: t.get("parent_id")}` alongside the existing `local_ticket_types`
  build (`outbound_differ.py:551`) and thread it into `_compute_outbound_update_mutation`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_parent_breadcrumb.py` (new) — in-process unit tests.

**Explicitly out of scope (with reason):** `pass_io.record_parent_divergence`
(`pass_io.py:80`) and its three call sites — `dispatch_one.py:558,569,579` and
`adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:158` — are **not** modified. They are the apply-time
`bridge_alerts` recorder; the signature is `(kind, key, local_id, parent, exc,
repo_root)` — scalar strings only, with `parent` being the *failed* parent key (or a
CLEAR sentinel), and no access to the local ticket graph, the binding store, the
transport comment client, or the Jira comment snapshot. The `acli_cli_ops.py:158` site
additionally passes `local_id=None` (`_attach_parent_guarded` is at the transport
boundary and carries no graph), so it structurally cannot supply the breadcrumb inputs.
The differ seam detects the same class of drift earlier, with all four inputs present, so
the breadcrumb is hosted there and these sites are left unchanged.

**Scope decision — UPDATE path only.** The breadcrumb is emitted only from the bound
(UPDATE) path: it requires the child's Jira issue to exist so a comment can be posted and
deduped against the child's Jira comment snapshot. On the pass where the child is first
created its parent is dropped at birth (`_compute_outbound_create_mutation` →
`dropped_field_sink`), but there is no child Jira key yet; the breadcrumb is then emitted
on the next pass once the child is bound and appears in the snapshot. The CREATE path is
therefore intentionally not touched.

## Testing

All tests are in-process unit tests over `_build_parent_breadcrumb` / `_diff_comments`
with a stub binding store (`get_jira_key`) and synthetic comment snapshots — the logic is
pure (ancestor walk, tag dedup, body assembly, marker decoration); the oracle is the
returned comment-mutation set / body text and the inbound classifier's verdict.

- **Breadcrumb emitted (happy path):** a bound child whose direct parent is a non-epic
  with a bound Jira key ⇒ exactly one `"add"` mutation whose body contains the parent's
  Jira key, the `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` tag, and the `RECONCILER_MARKER`.
- **Append-once / idempotent:** given a snapshot that already contains a breadcrumb-tagged
  comment (naming *any* ancestor) ⇒ no new mutation (tag-based dedup, not body-based),
  covering both a re-run and a changed-nearest-ancestor pass.
- **Unrepresented intervening ancestor noted:** the direct parent is unbound
  (`get_jira_key -> None`) and the walk skips to a higher ancestor that *is* bound ⇒ the
  body names that ancestor's key and states that one or more intervening parent levels
  are not represented in Jira.
- **Omitted when no bound ancestor (failure/empty path):** no ancestor in the chain has a
  bound Jira key ⇒ no mutation (nothing to point at).
- **Echo-safe:** the produced breadcrumb body, presented inbound, is skipped by
  `inbound_collection_diffs._diff_comments_inbound` because it carries `RECONCILER_MARKER`
  (asserted on the inbound mutation set being empty for that body).

## Body content contract

The breadcrumb body is deterministic (no timestamps or volatile content, so dedup is
stable). Concrete form, nearest represented ancestor = `PROJ-42`:

```
This ticket's parent hierarchy could not be fully represented in Jira. Nearest tracked ancestor: PROJ-42. Full parent context is maintained in rebar.
<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->

<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->
```

When one or more intervening ancestors were skipped because they lack a bound Jira key,
the sentence `One or more intervening parent levels are not represented in Jira.` is
inserted before `Full parent context...`. The first line never starts with an
`_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` value, so the comment is mirrored outbound (not machine-
excluded); the trailing `RECONCILER_MARKER` (added by `_decorate_outbound_comment`)
guarantees inbound suppression.

## Accepted limitations

- **No supersede/edit of a stale breadcrumb.** The outbound comment path is ADD-only and
  no transport-portable comment edit/delete exists; if the nearest represented ancestor
  changes across passes, tag-based dedup keeps the original breadcrumb and appends no
  second one. The original remains a valid "context lives upward, see rebar" pointer.
  This is preferred over emitting conflicting duplicate hints.

## Portability

The mechanism is in-process differ logic plus the existing `TicketTransport` comment port
(`add_comment` / `get_comments`), implemented by both supported backends
(`adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`). It introduces no
dependency on any specific CI system, no new binary, no new filesystem assumption, and no
new transport capability, so it runs identically across the library / CLI / MCP surfaces
and both Jira deployments. When `local_parents`/`local_ticket_types` are absent (a
non-parent-aware caller) the breadcrumb is a no-op, so no client shape regresses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bound child with a type-collapsed, bound parent appends exactly one echo-safe
  breadcrumb naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key and carrying both the
  `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` tag and `RECONCILER_MARKER` — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_emitted`.
- [ ] The breadcrumb is append-once via the stable identity tag, including when the
  nearest represented ancestor changes across passes (no conflicting second comment) —
  verified by `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_idempotent_and_supersede`.
- [ ] When the walk skips an unbound (unrepresented) intervening ancestor to reach a
  bound one, the body names the bound ancestor and states the intervening levels are not
  represented — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_unrepresented_intervening_ancestor_noted`.
- [ ] No ancestor with a bound Jira key ⇒ no breadcrumb mutation — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_omitted_when_no_bound_ancestor`.
- [ ] The breadcrumb body is suppressed inbound by `_diff_comments_inbound` because it
  carries `RECONCILER_MARKER` (not re-ingested as a user comment) — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_echo_safe`.

Test tier: **in-process unit** — the ancestor walk, tag dedup, body assembly, marker
decoration, and inbound classification are pure functions; oracles are the produced
comment mutation set / body and the inbound classifier verdict.
